beats.say: A jet engine is basically a tube that swallows air and turns it into a huge push.
First, a giant fan at the front sucks in air. A lot of it flows around the outside, and the rest goes into the core.
Inside, rows of spinning blades squeeze that air into a much smaller space. Squeezed air is packed tight and hot.
Then fuel is sprayed in and lit. The burning gas expands fiercely, with nowhere to go but backward.
On its way out, the hot gas spins a turbine, like a windmill. A shaft links it to the fan and the blades, so the engine powers itself.
Then the gas blasts out the back, much faster than it came in.
This is Newton's third law. Push gas backward, and the gas pushes the engine forward.
That forward push is called thrust. The engine is bolted to the plane, so the whole plane moves.
Open the throttle, and more fuel burns, more gas leaves, and the push grows.
